controls.object: The same E_p(F_p) and every sorted degree-4 divisor, for all four primes.
controls.procedure: Use an independent affine chord/tangent group implementation and O branches. For P+Q: O is identity; if xP=xQ and yP+yQ=0 return O; otherwise slope=(yQ-yP)/(xQ-xP) for distinct x, or (3*xP^2+1)/(2*yP) for doubling. Set xR=slope^2-xP-xQ, yR=slope*(xP-xR)-yP. Sum in the frozen order (((P1+P2)+P3)+P4). Confirm associativity by all triples on each complete finite group before using it as oracle.
controls.expected: Exactly the divisors satisfying sum=O correspond to rank-3 jet matrices and to fully split sections. Weighted relation total N_p^3. Equality and all control predicates must hold exactly; no numerical tolerance.

controls.object: Same D, basis and normalized coefficient c, presented in the original plane coordinates with its O chart.
controls.procedure: Use f_c=c0+c1*x+c2*y+c3*x^2 restricted to y^2=x^3+x+1, with identical jets, rationality, multiplicity and normalization. Compare this complete presentation against the quartic coordinates; never compare against an unrelated x-only Semaev polynomial.
controls.expected: Exact same accepted (D,c) pairs. This is the established linear-equivalence baseline and must be reproduced before the strictness comparison.

controls.object: At p=5: X=[1:0:0:0], c=[0:0:0:1], and the purported divisor 4[X].
controls.expected: Every ordinary linear row gives c dot X=0 and Q1(X)=0, but Q2(X)=-1=4 mod 5. Reject before recovery. Certificate contains X,c, linear residual 0 and curve-membership residual 4.
controls.known_false: This X is not a point of the original elliptic curve; ambient linearity cannot certify a relation.

controls.object: At p=5 on E:y^2=x^3+x+1, c=[1:4:0:0], the normalized section 1-x (same zero set as x-1).
controls.expected: The affine support satisfies x=1 and y^2=3, which has no F5 root (squares are 0,1,4). O has multiplicity 2; unresolved degree is 2. Reject as a split F5 relation while retaining that it is a rational section with extension-field support. Certificate lists the square-residue witness, O multiplicity and unresolved degree.
controls.known_false: Rational coefficients do not force all divisor points individually rational.

controls.expected: All four ordinary evaluation rows vanish; with t=x at P the section is t^2, so coefficient [t^2] is 1 and the required order-4 condition fails. Recovered divisor is 2[(0,1)]+2[(0,4)]. Reject the claimed pair (4[P],c). Independently check the group sum of 4[P]; the controlled expected value is (3,4), not O, obtained from the frozen group-law formulas, not a run result.
controls.known_false: A repeated point needs derivative/jet rows. Rank deficiency of duplicated point rows alone does not establish the relation.

controls.expected: Recover D=4[O], with rank-3 A_D and a one-dimensional kernel. At O, c0*u^2 has order 4. Rejecting this indicates a pole-deficit or projective-chart error.
Recover precisely this degree-4 divisor with multiplicity two on each affine point; its group sum is O.

controls.object: At p=5 use Eprime:y^2=x^3+x+2, iota prime=[1:x:y:x^2], Q1 unchanged and Q2prime=X2^2-X1*X3-X0*X1-2*X0^2. Enumerate every normalized c in dual P3(F5) and apply the identical section-recovery, jet and presentation measurements on Eprime.
controls.procedure: Use the same dimension 3, embedding degree 4, divisor degree 4 and field. When checking whether an Eprime divisor is an E divisor, apply the original E membership equations to each recovered point, without retargeting the curve constant.
controls.expected: Every finite Eprime point fails original membership by residual 1. The common 4[O] section is explicitly allowed; do not demand a rejection there. In particular c=[1:4:0:0] recovers (1,2)+(1,3)+2[O] on Eprime; both finite points have original E residual 1. Linear-system dimension and low degree alone must not certify an E relation. Comparison counts on Eprime are descriptive controls, not an ECDLP conclusion.
